Samira Ali: Quick Q 
 I left Redwood in Jan and was rehired this month. During exit I rolled my 401(k) to an IRA. My question: does my prior service count toward the plan's vesting schedule for employer match now that I'm back? Also, while I was gone I had an HSA with a small balance 
 can I keep using that for reimbursements even though payroll HSA contributions stopped while I was off?

Noah Kim: Welcome back! Short answers: vesting continuity depends on the plan's break-in-service rules. Some plans count prior service if rehire occurs within 5 years (or plan-specified period) without a break-in-service; others restart vesting after a separation that exceeds the threshold. We need your original hire date and separation date to check.

Rory (Benefits): Adding vendor detail: because you rolled out your 401(k) to an IRA, you no longer have an active account balance at the recordkeeper, but vesting is a plan-level metric tied to your service accrual history. If the plan treats your separation as a break-in-service (per plan doc), prior service might not count for future employer match vesting. Provide dates and well confirm with plan admin.

Samira Ali: I was originally hired 2018-06-12 and my termination was 2025-01-31. Rehire date 2026-02-15. That's 1 year and 15 days gap.

Rory (Benefits): Thanks 
 that timeframe usually preserves past service for vesting under our current plan (12-month break threshold is common, but plan doc controls). Ill escalate to plan admin to get written confirmation. If prior service counts, your prior vesting percentage will be restored; if not, vesting may restart at rehire. Well confirm.

PayrollBot: Automated: "Payroll/benefits note: employer match contributions only apply to deferrals made while you are on payroll. Past matches previously made (and vested) remain with your account unless distributed. If you rolled out your balance, any vested employer match already distributed remains subject to the receiving IRA's terms"

Samira Ali: For HSA reimbursements 
 my HSA is still at my bank with a $420 balance. Can I submit receipts and get reimbursed even if I'm not yet back on payroll HSA?

Rory (Benefits): Yes, your HSA is individually owned and can be used for qualified medical reimbursements regardless of employment status. You can pay qualified expenses from that account or request reimbursement from the HSA custodian. Payroll HSA contributions stopped during separation; to restart pre-tax payroll contributions you must enroll in HSA-eligible coverage and set payroll deferrals after rehire.

Samira Ali: If plan admin confirms prior service counts, will I be eligible for match retroactively for the months I was rehired but before I re-enrolled in deferrals?

Rory (Benefits): Employer match is never retroactive to past unpaid periods. Match applies on actual payroll contributions. If you were not contributing in a specific pay period (e.g., before updating elections), there is no match to credit for that period. However, if you reenroll and want to approximate missed savings, you can increase your deferral percentage going forward (within IRS limits) to catch up on savings, but match will only apply to new contributions.

Samira Ali: OK makes sense. Please confirm vesting with plan admin and let me know if I should send any forms. Thanks!

Rory (Benefits): Will do. Filing plan admin inquiry now and will post the written confirmation here when we get it. If plan admin needs paperwork, well ask. Welcome back :tada:

hr-bot: Policy snippet: "Rehire and break-in-service treatment for vesting and eligibility follows the plan document. HSAs are participant-owned and reimbursements can be made independent of employer payroll. Employer match applies only to payroll-withheld contributions."
